video_title: Stephen A.: Jalen Brunson was UNSTOPPABLE! 🤩 + Perk & Wilbon on Cavs in ECF Game 1 | SportsCenter

quotes.speaker: Stephen A. Smith
quotes.summary_phrase: Jalen Brunson's offensive explosion against James Harden
quotes.excerpt: Jalen Brunson goes ballistic and literally should be arrested for the assault that he put on James Harden.
quotes.quote: Relieved Nicole, absolutely relieved. I mean, they looked absolutely awful for more than three quarters of the game, and then after that, it was seven minutes left, they were down 22, and then all of a sudden Jalen Brunson goes ballistic and literally should be arrested for the assault that he put on James Harden. Just abused him at every single turn, annihilated him, kept going by him, scored like five or six straight baskets, and then it got to a point where seemingly anybody, whether it was Mikal Bridges, whether it was Brunson, whether it was Landry Shamet, anybody who attempted a shot, it was James Harden in the vicinity. It ain't just Jalen Brunson that should be arrested for assault, it's the rest of the Knicks because everybody at that point was targeting James Harden because he couldn't stop a cold. It was just that simple. But up before then, up before the seven-minute mark, when they were down by 22, they looked beyond rusty, they looked lethargic like they had been chilling for the last nine days, eating pizza and Lord knows what else. They did not look like the New York Knicks we had seen when seven straight playoff games, but thank goodness it didn't last the entire game.

quotes.speaker: Stephen A. Smith
quotes.summary_phrase: Cavaliers' Game 1 collapse was a demoralizing choke job
quotes.excerpt: It was unquestionably a choke job, make no mistake about it. It was a choke job.
quotes.quote: It was unquestionably a choke job, make no mistake about it. It was a choke job. You can't collapse like that. Where was Donovan Mitchell in the last seven minutes to stop the bleeding? He was nowhere to be found. James Harden was getting abused by every Knick in sight. You end up losing a 22-point lead, you end up spending the last seven minutes of regulation and overtime getting outscored 44 to 11. That is a demoralizing situation to be in, especially when you came to New York just to get one. In all likelihood, I can't imagine them getting Game 2. They're going to be in an 0-2 hole and it's going to be virtually impossible to imagine them doing what they did against Detroit, winning four of the last five games to win this series and get to the NBA Finals. I'd be shocked if a team this demoralized, clearly and visibly, is going to come back from a defeat of this nature. It's not just a loss, it's how you lose like that. This is a devastating loss.

quotes.speaker: Kendrick Perkins
quotes.summary_phrase: James Harden's defensive liability in Cavaliers' Game 1 loss
quotes.excerpt: James Harden was a defensive liability once again.

text_blocks.speaker: Michael Eaves
text_blocks.text: During the Knicks' 44 to 11 run to close out the game, Donovan Mitchell and James Harden were combined one for 10 from the floor, zero for five from three, two turnovers. They combined for three points. Donovan Mitchell's last made field goal came with 8:19 left in the fourth quarter. Please, sir, explain that to me.

text_blocks.speaker: Kendrick Perkins
text_blocks.text: Well, look, Eaves, first of all, good to see you and I'm loving the beard. Hello Nicole, good to see you as well. But let me say this, it's two sides of the basketball, right? I'm not disagreeing with you, they were awful offensively, but you're up double digits in the fourth quarter, all you have to do is get stops. And James Harden was a defensive liability once again. The Knicks were scoring on him at will. The entire Knicks squad was nine for 15 in the fourth quarter and overtime when James Harden was the defender. Jalen Brunson was seven for eight on James Harden. At some point, if you're Kenny Atkinson, you have to see this and you have to make a business decision and get him off the damn floor. It was less than a minute and a half in the game and he left strong side corner three and went did a half trap on Jalen Brunson and gave up a wide open three-point shot to Mikal Bridges. Here we are again. Different series, same story. James Harden, more turnovers than field goals made.

text_blocks.speaker: Nicole Briscoe
text_blocks.text: Okay, so I do want to move on a little bit. It's sort of on the same thing because it deals with coaching.

quotes.speaker: Kendrick Perkins
quotes.summary_phrase: Jason Kidd's departure from Mavericks signals more changes ahead
quotes.excerpt: J. Kidd is just the first domino to fall.

text_blocks.speaker: Nicole Briscoe
text_blocks.text: We did get some NBA news tonight, the Mavs and Jason Kidd, they're no more after five seasons. Kidd is out. It's described as a mutual decision. This also comes two weeks after the Mavs hired their new president, Masai Ujiri. So what do you think of that?

text_blocks.speaker: Kendrick Perkins
text_blocks.text: Well, this was way past due. This relationship had been run its course. J. Kidd wanted out of Dallas last year once they traded Luka. He's not a coach just with the rebuilding. He's a coach that wants to win championships. And so when you think about where they're headed, they traded Anthony Davis. Yes, he did an outstanding job for us building up and putting Cooper Flag in the right position, but J. Kidd is a coach that wants to win now. He is not looking in the near future or looking down the line five or six years from now. And so he wanted to go his own separate ways and rightfully so. And I'm going to say this, J. Kidd is just the first domino to fall. I wouldn't be surprised in the next two to three weeks if we see some more movement in the Mavericks organization for a guy named Kyrie Irving.

text_blocks.speaker: Michael Eaves
text_blocks.text: Rebuild, restructure, whatever you want to call it, a lot of moves down there.

quotes.speaker: Michael Wilbon
quotes.summary_phrase: Cavaliers' coaching blunders and dumb mistakes in Game 1 collapse
quotes.excerpt: How do you give up an 18 to one run and not call a timeout?

text_blocks.speaker: Michael Eaves
text_blocks.text: We can't get enough perspective about what we saw in Game 1 of the Eastern Conference Finals. So we bring in the Hall of Famer Mike Wilbon to get us a little more. And Mike, look, you've been around this league for decades and you've seen some crazy endings. But I need you to give me some perspective on exactly what we witnessed here. You witnessed firsthand how the Knicks looked like nothing and the Cavs looked like everything and then that completely switched by the time we got to the end of overtime.

text_blocks.speaker: Michael Wilbon
text_blocks.text: 20-point lead with seven plus minutes to play. Michael and Nicole, you don't say it's over, but it's pretty close to over. Cleveland is in control of the game. They're completely in control of the game. Cleveland was doing everything right until they did then did everything not just wrong, but dumb. I mean, just one stupid mistake after another. How do you give up an 18 to one run and not call a timeout? I can tell you the Knicks were surprised. Cleveland has four timeouts and doesn't call a timeout on an 18 to one run and wound up giving up 40 of the next 51 points in fourth quarter and overtime and wound up continuing to put James Harden, who 10 years ago, a much more athletic, capable James Harden couldn't guard Jalen Brunson. And now to put James Harden on Jalen Brunson time after time to let the Knicks dictate that matchup. It's just it's baffling and stupid to do that. It's unbelievable that a team as well as Cleveland had played, they had done everything right for such a long period of time. No one knows what the hell the Cleveland Cavaliers are doing after that seven and a half minute mark in the fourth quarter to the end of this game.

text_blocks.speaker: Nicole Briscoe
text_blocks.text: You know, when the game started though, the thought was that the Knicks have been they've been off, they've been resting, they're rusty. At the end, there was a part of my brain that switched to, well, Cleveland just came off a seven-game series. Now they're exhausted, they're tired. Stephen A. said, this is a team that's now like demoralized. I don't know. The question now is, do you do you see them coming back? How do they do that after what they did here?

quotes.speaker: Michael Wilbon
quotes.summary_phrase: Cavaliers' Game 1 loss reveals deep issues and lack of resilience
quotes.excerpt: It would say something about their nerve and guts and the most overused word in sports today, resilience.

text_blocks.speaker: Nicole Briscoe
text_blocks.text: Do you do you see them coming back? How do they do that after what they did here?

text_blocks.speaker: Michael Wilbon
text_blocks.text: No, I don't see them coming back to win a game, Nicole. Let's go back to the part, a great point you raised about coming off a seven-game series, a tough grueling seven-game series previously with Detroit. So why do you not call timeout during an 18-1 run when you got four of them? You don't call timeout, you know your guys are likely to be tired. Or as one Hall of Famer here in attendance said to me, he had to know their legs are shot. Why do you not call timeout? Why do you have James Harden still out there? What is it you're trying to do with Brunson? And it's just one question after another which has no reasonable answer after another.

text_blocks.speaker: Michael Eaves
text_blocks.text: And here's the thing. I said this earlier. I don't care who wins or loses these games. I have no vested interest. But as a basketball fan, I was offended how the Cavs finished that game and all the things you raised. And now they got to somehow respond and try to whatever. Game 2 Thursday, 8 Eastern, ESPN. At least we get to watch it together because I don't know what's going to happen.

text_blocks.speaker: Nicole Briscoe
text_blocks.text: I will say this, if they do respond, it does say something about them that I don't think any of us expect.

text_blocks.speaker: Michael Wilbon
text_blocks.text: It would say something about their nerve and guts and the most overused word in sports today, resilience. But I don't see any of that happening. You know, and did we see Donovan limping off the court? Was he limping? A little limp to his gait when he went through the tunnel. If that's the case, what is it they have? What is it they're going to resort to? What is it they're going to rely on?

text_blocks.speaker: Michael Eaves
text_blocks.text: Then they got no chance. They got zero chance on that.
